title: iSEW: in-Sensor Embedded Watermarking for Secure Imaging
problem: Digital images lack hardware-native tamper resistance and are vulnerable to post-capture modifications. Current watermarking approaches operate post-acquisition, adding computational overhead and remaining susceptible to removal attacks.
motivation: Embedding watermarking directly at the sensor readout stage enables tamper-resistant image authentication at the point of capture with minimal overhead.
method: Analog-domain watermarking is embedded during the readout stage before ADC conversion in CMOS sensors. The column amplifier architecture is modified to inject the watermark, controlled by a secure pattern generator. The watermark is embedded at the pixel readout level, creating a hardware-native, low-overhead tamper-resistant mechanism.
key_novelty: Implementing watermark embedding at the analog readout stage before ADC, directly integrated into CMOS sensor circuitry, provides a hardware-native security primitive.
contributions: Analog-domain watermarking architecture integrated into CMOS sensor readout electronics
Modified column amplifier design enabling watermark injection with minimal overhead
Secure pattern generator for watermark control and embedding
Experimental validation achieving >85% detection rates with minimal image quality impact on 64×64 pixel arrays
